claim_rules.observed_difference: a delta between two paired formal runs, read against the print precision and the larger of the two sides' same-identity runtime-repeat observed ranges; 'above_runtime_repeat_range' means the instrument resolved it in this campaign
claim_rules.observed_range_zero: an observed range of 0.0 means this batch of repeat runs saw no variation (k = 1 distinct output in n runs bounds only per-run divergence rates above ~1-0.05^(1/n)); it is not a bound and not a determinism claim
claim_rules.effect_claim: not issued by this report: a delta above the runtime-repeat range is not by itself a causal effect; every row keeps its remaining_confounds; the C group is additionally read against the training-seed reference (D group) for attributability, and even where it exceeds that reference the statement is 'consistent across three seed-paired replicates', not an effect size
claim_rules.baseline_identity: baseline status is the contract pair's lhs by orientation; no row was chosen by ranking a metric
claim_rules.historical: plain-GT2 <-> T3->T1 in either family is not a prepared pair (warmup_epochs 5->3 outside the curriculum; s also differs in seed); quoted only under section 'historical'

variance_axes.runtime_repeat: same identity, repeated runs (repeat reports): what the measurement instrument resolves
variance_axes.training_seed: seed_replicate pairs (D1-D4): different checkpoints from the same recipe at different seeds; a training-process quantity
variance_axes.rule: never pooled and never substituted: a treatment delta is read against runtime_repeat for resolvability and against training_seed for attributability; a seed-replicate delta is not a runtime-repeat estimate and vice versa
